esfcu_cro_show_options.ai_response: Three paths, and they are not mutually exclusive. One: the targeted member warning alone — fastest to send, no member friction, but it depends on members reading it, so loss reduction is only moderate. Two: transfer step-up verification on the flagged patterns — the strongest single lever on loss, but it adds friction for every member who hits it, and the education community will feel that. Three: both, paired with closing the Howard University coverage gap — the recommendation, because the warning and the step-up contain the campaign while the coverage work removes the blind spot it is exploiting. Doing only one and two leaves the gap open for the next campaign.
